Through the analysis of $g(a)-g(b) \mid a^n-b^n$, I determined that $n$ is exotic if its odd part is a perfect square and the exponent of 2 in its prime factorization is either 0 or an odd number. This leads to the set of exotic integers being $\{n \mid n = 2^s k^2, \text{ where } k \text{ is odd and } s \in \{0, 1, 3, 5, \dots\}\}$. I verified this with a script and confirmed the 132nd exotic integer is 11881.
